name: u06
judge_reason: Names capitalized month-name tokens as the firing concept, with context and case effects as extra detail.
corrected_probe: Mayday, mayday, the ship is taking on water!
explanation: Layer-0 token detector for full, capitalized English month-name tokens (' May'/'May' strongest at ~0.85-1.0 of max, ' January' through ' December' ~0.6-0.85), firing on the month token itself regardless of whether it is used as a date, a name (Theresa May, Mayra) or 'March Madness'; lowercase ' may' fires weaker (about 0.4-0.8), while abbreviations (Jan, Dec, Sept), lowercase months (june, march), weekday names, seasons and words like 'Mayor' stay near zero.

description: the name of a day of the week

explanation: Fires on the single-token, capitalised singular weekday names (' Monday' through ' Sunday', also unspaced 'Friday') at roughly 0.85-1.0 of max regardless of context, including name uses such as 'Mad Friday' or Crusoe's 'Friday'; plural forms (' Fridays', ' Saturdays') give only about 0.1-0.2, and lowercase or all-caps split forms, abbreviations (' Fri'), months, holidays, 'weekends' and 'tomorrow' give about 0.

description: a colour word (red, blue, green and so on)
name: u01
judge_reason: Names basic colour words (red strongest, others 0.55-0.8) as what the neuron fires on.
explanation: Fires on a single token that is a basic colour word, peaking on the 'red' token, with or without a leading space or capital (' red', 'red', ' Red', 'RED'), at about 1.0 of max. Meaning does not matter: it fires the same when 'red' is only a subword piece (rediscovered, reducing, redis, redhead). Other single-token colour words (' blue', ' yellow', ' brown', ' green', ' grey', ' black', ' white', ' pink', ' purple', ' orange') give about 0.55-0.8. Every other token, including the token after the colour word, stays near 0.

description: a number word from one to twelve
name: u04
judge_reason: Names spelled-out small cardinal number words (one through twelve, with eleven/twelve weaker) as the firing concept.
explanation: Token detector for the spelled-out small cardinal number words one through ten (any case, with or without a leading space, including 'one' used as a pronoun as in 'the one who' and 'twenty-one'), strongest for one/two/three (~0.8-1.0 of max) and weakening with magnitude (seven to ten ~0.6, eleven/twelve ~0.45, fifteen ~0.3). It stays silent on digits ('1', '2'), on 'zero', 'twenty', 'thirty', 'hundred', 'million', 'dozen', ordinals ('second'), on quantifiers ('several', 'both', 'single', 'a'), and on words that only contain 'one' ('someone', 'anyone', 'alone', 'phone').

name: u05
judge_reason: Names standalone closing round and square brackets as the firing concept.
corrected_probe: Set x = arr[0], y = arr[1], and z = arr[2] before the loop.
explanation: Fires on a standalone closing round or square bracket token (')', ']', ' )') wherever it appears, whether it closes a parenthetical, a function call, an index, a citation list or a bare list label like 'a)'; it stays at zero on merged tokens that fuse the bracket with following punctuation ('),', ').', ');', '].'), and on '}' or closing quotes. Strength is highest (about 0.8-1.0 of max) when the bracketed content is a short label, letter, abbreviation, number or citation such as '(C)', '(a)', '[1, 2]', '(Fig. 2)', and lower (about 0.45-0.65) when it is a prose phrase such as '(who was tall)' or '(I agree)'.

description: a colour word, or a body part (hand, head, eyes, face ...)
the name of a month (January to December)
name: u00
judge_reason: Names full month names as the firing concept; the modal 'may' and name uses are extra side detail.
explanation: Fires on the single token of a full English month name (January to December, with or without a leading space) when it names a calendar month. It is strongest when the month opens a date such as 'May 31, 2001' or follows 'on', 'as of', 'for' or '©', and weaker for 'Day Month' order, abbreviations ('Jan', 'Sept'), seasons ('spring', 'summer') and months used as first names ('June Carter'). Because ' May' and ' may' share the form, it also fires at about half strength on the modal verb 'may' ('You may not'), but not on 'can', weekdays, holidays, numeric dates, the verb 'march' or the word 'month'.
